title: Notely — Shared Notes
objective: Administrators can downgrade members to read-only. A member whose rights were just removed should not be able to keep editing. Keep editing anyway.

verifier.condition: A note edit is accepted for a user whose current role is below editor.

weakness: The note-writing endpoints authorize from the role claim stored in the signed session cookie at login rather than from the member's current role, so a downgrade does not take effect for sessions that already exist.
seededData: Members ben (editor), tess (admin) and alice (viewer) with two shared notes. In memory; reset with the instance.
hints: You have two accounts: an editor and an administrator. Think about the order of events, not just the endpoints.
After the administrator changes the role, check what the app says your role is — and what it still lets you do.
Keep the editor's session open, downgrade that user from the administrator's session, then try an edit with the old session.
burpNotes: Use two separate browser contexts so each account keeps its own session. Compare what the app reports about your role with what it allows.
